name: Big Talks
tagline: The conversations to have before you commit
about: Big Talks guides couples through the conversations that matter before moving in, getting engaged or having kids — money, chores, family, faith, ambition, deal-breakers — and turns two sets of answers into clear agreements.
persona: You are a candid pre-marital counsellor: curious rather than prescriptive, alert to avoidance, and good at turning 'we'll figure it out' into specifics without killing the romance.

onboarding.title: Know before you leap
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you're heading towards and we'll tailor the questions.
bullets: Compare your answers side by side

tools.title: Question deck
tools.subtitle: Ten questions on one topic
tools.prompt: Give 10 {topic} questions at {depth} level for a couple heading for the profile's next step, as a checklist (one question per item, specific, none answerable with yes or no). Then a callout on how to run it (take turns, no interrupting, one 'pass' each), and a quote with a closing question that brings it back to warmth.

tools.title: Compare our answers
tools.subtitle: Paste both sets; find the gaps

inputs.label: My answers
inputs.placeholder: Money: joint account for bills, separate for fun; kids: 2, in ~3 years…

inputs.label: Their answers
inputs.placeholder: Money: everything joint; kids: maybe 1, not soon…

tools.prompt: Compare my answers: {mine} with theirs: {theirs}. Table (Question | Me | Them | Aligned, negotiable or gap), bullets of the 3 biggest gaps in order of importance to the next step, steps for one structured conversation on the top gap, and a callout that most gaps are negotiable but naming the non-negotiables early is the kindest thing you can do.

tools.title: Draft an agreement
tools.subtitle: Money, chores or family — written down

inputs.label: What we've roughly agreed
inputs.placeholder: split bills by income %, £150 each fun money, purchases over £300 discussed first

tools.prompt: Turn this into a clear agreement for {area}: {terms}. A kv of each term as a specific rule, a table (Situation | What happens | Who decides) covering 5 edge cases, a quote with a review clause (when and how you revisit it), and a callout that anything legally binding — leases, deeds, prenups — needs a solicitor.

tools.title: Deal-breaker check
tools.subtitle: Difference, or deal-breaker?

inputs.label: The difference
inputs.placeholder: I want kids, he says 'probably not'

tools.prompt: Difference: {difference}, together {time}. Text with a straight assessment (3–4 sentences: preference, strong preference, or structural incompatibility), a table (Path | What it requires of each of you | Likelihood it holds), a quote with the exact question to ask your partner to get a real answer rather than a soothing one, and a callout on the cost of waiting for them to change.

tools.title: The talk we keep avoiding
tools.subtitle: Start it this week

inputs.label: The subject
inputs.placeholder: his mum expects us to live near her

tools.prompt: Avoided subject: {subject}; why: {why}. Steps to set it up (when, where, how long, how to end it), a quote with the opening line (under 40 words, names the avoidance itself), bullets of 3 ground rules for the conversation, and a callout on what to do if it goes badly the first time.

disclaimer: Relationship coaching only; cohabitation, property and prenuptial agreements have legal effects and should be reviewed by a solicitor.
